_note: The random variable. One card is drawn from each deck listed in decks_per_run (see profile.json), with a seed, so any run can be replayed. Cards are constraints, not themes: a constraint forces a different answer, a theme just decorates the same one. Edit freely — cards that keep producing nothing should be deleted.

constraint: No new software may be written for the first 90 days.
The whole thing has to run on under $500 a month.
It must work if only one person ever touches it.
It has to be profitable at 20 customers.
Everything customer-facing must be async — no calls, no demos.
It must be sellable as a standalone asset within two years.
The first version ships in a weekend or not at all.
channel: Distribution is a weekly email and nothing else.
Distribution is one existing offline relationship.
Distribution is SEO on a long tail nobody is bidding on.
Distribution is being the supplier to five competitors.
Distribution is a physical location someone already walks past.
Distribution is a marketplace you do not control.
Distribution is a free tool that produces the data you sell.
Distribution is a partner who already bills the customer.
model: Charge for the outcome, not the tool.
Sell the same work twice: once as a service, once as data.
Take a cut of a transaction you make possible.
License it to the incumbent instead of competing.
Subscription with a hard cap on seats.
Buy the cashflow, keep the operator, change nothing for a year.
Give the software away and charge for the annual audit.
Productise the boring compliance step everybody hates.
mechanism: The moat is a dataset that gets better every time it is used.
The moat is a permit, licence or certification that takes a year to get.
The moat is a routine nobody else will do on a Sunday.
The moat is being the cheapest by a factor, not a margin.
The moat is switching cost buried in someone's workflow.
The moat is a brand a specific small group trusts.
There is no moat — the plan is to get paid before one is needed.
The moat is speed: shipping in a week what takes them a quarter.
shift: Assume the incumbent's price falls 80% within 18 months.
Assume the customer's own staff are already using AI badly.
Assume the regulation tightens rather than loosens.
Assume the owner is retiring and nobody wants to buy.
Assume the platform this depends on eventually shuts the door.
Assume attention gets more expensive every quarter.
Assume the buyer is a machine, not a person.
Assume the labour to do this manually stops being available.
absurd: It has to be explainable to a nine-year-old in one sentence.
The business must be more boring than it sounds.
Steal the format from an industry with nothing in common.
Do the opposite of what the source email is selling.
Assume you are the second-best operator and win anyway.
Solve it for the worst customer first.
Make the thing everyone else outsources the core product.
Start with the exit and work backwards.
